function.name: generate_report
function.description: Generates a comprehensive report based on user activity data within a specified time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier for the user.

start_date.description: The start date for the report period in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the report period, inclusive, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_inactive.description: Flag to determine if inactive users should be included in the report.

report_format.description: The format in which the report will be generated.

**Ionisation methods – a quick guide** | Ionisation technique | Typical application | Key advantages | Common limitations | |----------------------|---------------------|----------------|--------------------| | **Electron Impact (EI)** | Gas‑phase mass spectrometry (GC‑MS) | • Simple, robust;
• Produces reproducible fragmentation patterns;
• Good for volatile, thermally stable compounds | • Requires high vacuum;
• Not suitable for large, labile molecules | | **Chemical Ionisation (CI)** | GC‑MS, some LC‑MS | • Softer than EI → less fragmentation;
• Useful for polar, thermally labile analytes | • Still needs GC;
• Lower sensitivity for very non‑polar compounds | | **Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionisation (APCI)** | LC‑MS, especially for small, semi‑polar molecules | • Operates at atmospheric pressure → minimal sample prep;
• Good for moderately polar analytes | • Less effective for highly polar or large biomolecules | | **Electrospray Ionisation (ESI)** | LC‑MS, proteomics, metabolomics | • Very soft → preserves intact ions;
• Handles large biomolecules (proteins, nucleic acids);
• Amenable to high‑throughput workflows | • Requires aqueous or polar solvents;
• Suppression effects in complex matrices | | **Matrix‑Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionisation (MALDI)** | Proteomics, polymers, large biomolecules | • Rapid analysis;
• Minimal sample prep;
• Handles very large molecules | • Requires matrix;
• Limited to solid samples | | **Photoionisation (PI)** | GC‑MS, environmental analysis | • Non‑destructive;
• Good for non‑polar, volatile compounds | • Requires UV source;
• Lower sensitivity for polar compounds | | **Field‑Ionisation (FII)** | High‑resolution MS, large biomolecules | • Ultra‑soft;
• Minimal fragmentation | • Requires specialized equipment;
• Lower throughput | | **Laser Ablation (LA)** | Solid samples, imaging MS | • Direct sampling of solids;
• Spatially resolved analysis | • Requires laser system;
• Can cause fragmentation | ### How to choose the “best” method? 1. **Sample type & state** - *Volatile, thermally stable*: EI or CI (GC‑MS). - *Large biomolecules (proteins, peptides)*: ESI or MALDI. - *Solid or tissue imaging*: LA or MALDI imaging. 2. **Desired information** - *Structural elucidation*: EI (rich fragmentation). - *Molecular weight determination*: ESI, MALDI, or APCI (soft ionisation). 3. **Matrix effects & sensitivity** - ESI is prone to ion suppression in complex matrices; use cleanup or alternative ionisation (APCI). - MALDI can suffer from matrix interference; careful matrix selection is key. 4. **Instrumentation & throughput** - EI and CI are standard on GC‑MS; ESI/APCI on LC‑MS. - MALDI is fast but requires a MALDI‑MS instrument. 5. **Regulatory or safety constraints** - Some ionisers (e.g., EI) involve high‑energy electrons; ensure proper shielding. ### Quick decision tree ``` ┌─ Is the analyte volatile and thermally stable? ──► EI (GC‑MS) │ ├─ Is it a large biomolecule (protein, peptide)? ──► ESI (LC‑MS) or MALDI │ ├─ Is it a solid or tissue sample? ──► MALDI imaging or LA‑MS │ └─ Is it a polar, non‑volatile compound? ──► APCI (LC‑MS) or CI (GC‑MS) ``` --- **Bottom line:** There isn’t a single “best” ionisation method—each is optimized for different classes of analytes and analytical goals. Match the technique to your sample’s physical/chemical properties, the information you need, and the instrumentation you have available. If you can share more about your specific application (e.g., type of sample, target analytes, required sensitivity), I can help narrow down the optimal choice.
